$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-DX-005 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §8.7 and the RF-DX-005 inventory entry. Expresses supporting-evidence / uncertainty STRUCTURE only: self-tests (e.g. ASLR, femoral nerve slump) may describe function or activate a neural differential but are NOT validated RF diagnostic or rule-out tests. A positive self-test does not rule in RF injury; a negative does not rule it out; cannot_assess / unsafe / incomplete results remain unresolved and are never converted to positive, negative, or clearance. Self-tests never proceed while safety is blocked. No diagnosis, rehab, dosage, progression, confidence, or return-to-sport logic; safety precedence preserved. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.

input_contract.$comment: Structural self-test inputs taken verbatim-in-meaning from v1.2 §8.7. Self-tests are recorded as supporting evidence only and only when safe to perform.

decision_contract.$comment: Supporting-evidence / uncertainty structure only. Self-test results never rule in or rule out RF injury, never assign weight/probability/confidence, and never become safety clearance. Unresolved results stay unresolved. No rehab authorization, no numeric values. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Mixed normative source; MUST; permitted_use logic_with_uncertainty. Architecture ref and evidence claims preserved per source: architecture V3.1-9 (self-test capability & reliability model); QRF-004 (I1), QRF-005 (I1). Per §8.7: ASLR and femoral nerve slump results may describe function or activate a neural differential but are NOT validated RF diagnostic or rule-out tests; apply the self-administration reliability model (V3.1 §9), and pain-invalidated and cannot_assess results remain unresolved. Per V3.1 §9.2 four prohibited inferences: a failed attempt is not positive; a not-performed test is not negative; a painful test is not automatically positive; unclear execution is not high-confidence evidence. Self-tests only proceed when the pre-test safety screen is clear and never while safety is blocked (V3.1 §7.3 / §9.1). Diagnosis supporting-evidence rule, not a safety rule, so safety_state_output is null and blocked_targets is empty; it preserves safety precedence and must not be treated as safety clearance. No diagnostic confidence model is authored here (deferred to the later confidence objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
